reason: The skin needs a water barrier, so I’ll combine the cell layers with the lipids between them.
expectation: I expect an outer skin layer that helps retain water.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels and connective tissue also seem useful for living skin, but I want to build the barrier first.

effect: The epidermal barrier slows water loss and renews itself, so I’ll build the supporting skin tissue next.
reaction: The link between deeper cells and replacement of shed surface cells was useful.
reason: Combining connective tissue with blood vessels seems like a practical next step toward living skin.
expectation: I expect a supported, blood-supplied layer beneath the epidermal barrier.

alternatives.reason: A complete sweat gland also seems useful, but I want to assemble the supporting tissue first.

effect: The connective tissue and vessels formed a vascular dermis, which can now be joined to the outer barrier.
reaction: The result was expected and makes the layer assembly clear.
reason: Joining the dermis and epidermal barrier should build the main skin layers.
expectation: I expect a layered skin structure with a blood-supplied dermis beneath the epidermis.

alternatives.reason: The sweat gland also needs assembly, but I want to join the main layers first.

effect: The epidermis and vascular dermis formed layered skin with slots for a sweat outlet and sensory endings.
reaction: The marked locations make the next fittings clear.
reason: I’ll assemble the sweat gland so it can connect to the skin’s sweat outlet.
expectation: I expect a sweat gland with a duct leading to an outlet.

alternatives.reason: The sensory endings also fit the skin, but I want to prepare the gland first.

effect: The gland and duct now form a route to a pore, ready to fit into the layered skin.
reaction: The result was expected and makes the sweat outlet easy to place.
reason: I’ll fit the assembled gland into the skin’s sweat outlet.
expectation: I expect the layered skin to contain the gland and its duct, with the sensory slot still open.

alternatives.reason: The sensory endings also fit, but I want to finish placing the gland first.

effect: The sweat gland is fitted into the layered skin, leaving the sensory endings to add.
reason: The sensory endings fill the remaining slot and support the goal of skin that can feel.
expectation: I expect skin containing both the sweat gland and sensory endings.

effect: The skin now has sensory endings as well as a sweat gland, and is ready to cover the body.
reaction: The explanation connects the skin’s parts to their roles, though the fitting was expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the goal of covering the body with living skin.
expectation: I expect the body to be covered with the assembled living skin.

effect: The completed skin now covers the body, with its vessels and nerves joining those inside it; the chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The result was expected and gave the assembled layers a clear place in the body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the epidermal barrier was most worthwhile because it connected the layers and lipids to water retention and explained how the surface renews itself.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the sweat gland was straightforward but added little explanation on its own; the later description made its position and outlet clearer.

surprise.text: The explanation that deeper cells replace those shed at the surface made skin renewal clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the named parts and slots gave each combination a clear purpose, though the compatible options made the choices predictable.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the assembled body works as a whole, although the predictable fittings made this chapter feel more like assembly than problem-solving.
